I’ll trace the failing drift script and the local package wiring around `@pantoken/translation-adapters`, then make the smallest fix that makes the CI command resolve the dependency in a fresh workspace.

content.text: Graph search returned a large result set; I’m just reading the top of it to avoid wandering. After that I’ll inspect the package metadata and the failing script side by side.

The failing import is a dev dependency of `@pantoken/web-components`, and its export points at `tools/translation-adapters/dist/index.mjs`. My working hypothesis is that CI runs `check:drift` before that private tool package has been packed, so Node follows the workspace symlink to an empty `dist`. I’m checking the task graph/build config now.

The root task `i18n:check:drift` directly runs the three package drift checks and currently has no dependency on the translation adapter build. I’m reading the rest of that task block and the adapter config to choose whether the fix belongs in the aggregate task or the package-level scripts.

There are three drift scripts with the same private tool dependency. The fix can be either task-graph level or script-level; I’m checking the CI invocation shape before editing so the change lands where the fresh-run contract actually lives.

The CI job runs only `vp run i18n:check:drift`, outside `ready:all`, so it doesn’t inherit `build:all`. I’m going to add a focused dependency from that aggregate drift task to the adapter’s build, which should make the exported `dist/index.mjs` exist before any of the three scripts import it.

I didn’t find an existing `dependsOn` example that targets a package task directly, so I’m using the repo’s established `vp run @package#task` form inside the aggregate command. That keeps the fix boring and matches the command style already in this file.

content.text: The first edit is in. I’m running the exact failed command now; this is the cheap falsifier for the hypothesis that the missing adapter build caused the CI error.

content.text: Only `vite.config.ts` changed, and the validation didn’t leave tracked build artifacts behind. I’m checking editor diagnostics for that file as a final local sanity pass.

Fixed the CI drift check by updating [vite.config.ts](vite.config.ts#L354) so `i18n:check:drift` first runs `vp run @pantoken/translation-adapters#build`. That ensures the private workspace package has `dist/index.mjs` before the web-components, scaffold, and AI drift scripts import `@pantoken/translation-adapters`.

Validation passed:

```sh
vp run i18n:check:drift
```

It packed `@pantoken/translation-adapters` and all three drift checks completed successfully. No editor diagnostics in [vite.config.ts](vite.config.ts).
